title: BIS says stablecoins compete with correspondent banks
excerpt:
🌑 NEW: Bank for International Settlements finds stablecoins compete with cross-border banking infrastructure.

Ethereum, Solana and Tron are identified as networks facilitating international stablecoin transfers without relying on correspondent banks or SWIFT messaging.

Researchers examine the "stablecoin sandwich," citing Félix Pago's U.S.–Mexico remittance service as a real-world application.

The findings show that stablecoin-based foreign exchange can approach wholesale market rates, while blockchain transaction fees are economically negligible.

title: Russia hits energy sites across 11 Ukrainian regions
excerpt:
BREAKING: Russia struck energy facilities across 11 Ukrainian regions overnight, one of the largest attacks on energy infrastructure of the war, Ukraine's Ministry of Energy and Zelensky says.

More than 10 energy sites and 28 substations were hit, leaving at least 550,000 homes without power.

Ukraine will respond. Zelensky said last week that "the main rule of our operations is to respond" after ending the pause on strikes on Russian energy.

author: @DoWCTO
title: War Department says 30 universities cut foreign research ties
excerpt:
The Department of War announced today the successful completion of its initial research security audits of 30 universities. All 30 universities have fully mitigated identified relationships with foreign entities of concern included on the most recent NDAA Section 1286 list, published in July 2026. Overall, the audits resulted in more than 80 termination-related actions across the 30 universities. These actions included the termination of relationships with entities on the NDAA Section 1286 list, as well as precautionary terminations involving entities not specifically identified on the list.

author: @USTreasury
title: FinCEN flags about $270 million in suspicious student-aid activity
excerpt:
Today, Treasury announced that @FinCENnews has identified approximately $270 million in suspicious financial activity potentially linked to fraud against federal student aid programs. FinCEN has referred these findings to federal investigators to pursue potential fraud schemes targeting federal student aid programs and help ensure those responsible are held accountable.

These referrals underscore the Trump Administration’s commitment to eliminating fraud, protecting taxpayers, and safeguarding the integrity of federal student aid programs.

author: @SecScottBessent
title: Bessent says Treasury will recover stolen student-aid funds
excerpt: Federal student aid is intended to expand educational opportunities, not line the pockets of fraudsters who steal from students pursuing their education and hardworking taxpayers. The Trump Administration will not tolerate criminals who exploit government programs for personal gain. Treasury is working with financial institutions and law enforcement to identify these fraud schemes, recover stolen funds, and hold those responsible accountable.
